title: Very near to you (Tanya, title page)
hookLine: the Tanya's subtitle is "the word is very nigh unto thee" (Deuteronomy 30:14)
tomorrow: why can't a sad wrestler win? the Tanya has an answer.

lines: THE ANSWER ON THE TITLE PAGE.
cards: Somewhere in a phone there is usually a someday list: the call to make when there's time, the habit for after exams, the thing to learn once life calms down. Someday keeps everything at arm's length.
So, yesterday's question: how far away is the good you're reaching for, really? The Tanya answers before its first chapter, on the title page, with a verse.

teach.h: NOT IN HEAVEN, NOT ACROSS THE SEA.
teach.b: The verse is from Moses' last speeches in Deuteronomy: "But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it."
Just before it, the Torah says the commandment isn't up in heaven, and it isn't across the sea.
The Tanya's title page says the whole book is built on that verse, to explain how it is very near, by a long way and by a short way.
That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: a book of Hasidic teaching opens by promising that the good is close, and then spends its pages showing how. Look at the three places the verse names.
In your mouth: what you say. In your heart: what you feel. That thou mayest do it: what your hands do.
The heart may pull the wrong way, yet the mouth and the hands are near enough to choose.

teach.h: A SENTENCE, A FEELING, A STEP.
teach.b: And look back at two weeks of lessons: Miriam's hope, Bityah's open arms, an answer sized for one child.
None of it needed a mountain. It was a sentence, a feeling, a step.

how: The Tanya is printed with its title page citing Deuteronomy 30:14, and Deuteronomy 30 is read in synagogue in the weeks before Rosh Hashanah.

games.q: what does “very near to you” mean?
o: within reach of your mouth, heart and hands
a feeling that God is watching over you
a holy place you can only reach by travel

games.q: where the word is — tap the pairs.

s: Deuteronomy says the commandment is up in heaven, for the holy few
it says the opposite: not in heaven, not across the sea, but very near.
the Tanya's title page builds the whole book on Deuteronomy 30:14
it promises to explain how the word is very near, by a long way and a short.

games.q: a friend says she'll start volunteering "once life calms down." by the verse on the Tanya's title page, what's the honest nudge?
o: it's nearer than that: one small piece, this week.
she's right; good deeds need a calm life first.
it's too far off for her now, so don't push it.
games.why: the word is very near: in your mouth, in your heart, that you may do it. the nearest piece is usually small.

practice: Name one good thing you've been keeping on the someday list: a call, an apology, a habit, a page of study. Find its nearest piece, a sentence you could say or one small thing your hands could do.
Decide exactly when, and see yourself doing it.

wordCard.voice: Very near to you: the verse on the Tanya's title page. The good is in your mouth, in your heart, and within reach of your hands.
